user.title: Welcome to SOSSEN Direct
user.description:
Your SOSSEN inverters in Home Assistant, read **locally** every ~5 s, with their power limit and a built-in overvoltage protection.

**You need:**
- your Smart Life (or PowerHome) **user code**: app → Me → ⚙️ Settings → Account and Security → User Code
- your **phone** to scan a QR code
- the inverters **powered on**: set up in daytime, they switch off at night

The account is only used to fetch the inverters and their local keys; data then flows over your LAN, not through the cloud.

behind_router.title: Inverters behind another router
behind_router.description:
When the inverters are on the Wi-Fi of a second router (repeater in router mode, NAT), Home Assistant cannot see them. On that router:

1. **Reserve an IP** for each inverter (DHCP reservation / static lease).
2. Create **one TCP port-forwarding rule per inverter**: external port 6668 → 1st inverter port 6668, external port 6669 → 2nd inverter port 6668, and so on.
3. List below the router's address with those ports, comma separated (e.g. `192.168.1.41:6668, 192.168.1.41:6669`). Each inverter is recognised by its key, the order does not matter.

protection.title: Overvoltage protection
protection.description:
Inverters typically disconnect from the grid around **253 V**, and the voltage rises by about **3.5 V per kW injected**. The protection lowers every power limit a little before that, and raises it back when the voltage drops.

Recommended values (the defaults): lower at **249 V**, raise at **245 V**, down by **70 W**, back up by **30 W**, every **120 s**, never below **500 W**.

You can change all this later in the integration options, or turn it on/off with its switch.

data_description.high_voltage: Highest AC voltage measured by the producing inverters.
data_description.step_down: Removed from every limit at each check while the voltage is too high.
data_description.step_up: Added back at each check once the voltage is low enough: smaller, so it does not oscillate.
data_description.interval: Each change is a command written to the inverter: keep it reasonable.

power.title: Power limits
power.description:
Set one limit for **all** inverters, or leave it blank and set each one below. Only changed values are sent.

While the overvoltage protection is on, it keeps adjusting these limits.

network.title: Network and addresses
network.description:

**Inverters behind another router:** reserve their IPs in that router's DHCP and create one TCP port-forwarding rule per inverter (external ports 6668, 6669, ... → port 6668 of each inverter), then list the router's addresses below (e.g. `192.168.1.41:6668, 192.168.1.41:6669`). Each inverter is recognised by its key.
